what_happened: While reading request 20261025-183644-t67q, the reader stopped at reading 1 and asked a question that neither the repo nor the defaults settled. The context is a check runner that switches to nextest. In the sandboxed check environment, the pinned tools directory was not visible. The check could therefore fall back to plain cargo test without anyone noticing. The user answered: pass the pinned-tools directory to checks explicitly (add ATHENA_HOME or the resolved tools path to the check's environment). Each test check must also record and print which runner it used (nextest or cargo test), so a fallback is never silent. The measured numbers and the nextest choice from the earlier correction stay, and doctests still run with cargo test --doc. The event was logged as a correction, but it was an answered question. No reading was wrong.
cause: The request chose a faster runner but did not settle the design policy behind it: how checks find pinned tools in a cleared environment, and whether a fallback may be silent. Nothing in the defaults states that a check's environment must be given its tool paths explicitly, or that a runner choice must be visible in the output. The reading step has no way to settle such a preference before the job starts, so it came up as a question. The related registry class, plan-ignores-check-runtime-environment (20261025-183616-zmkp), covers the same environment gap, but it fires later, in planning rounds. Here the gap surfaced early, as a question.
prevention: Add a written default: a check never depends on inherited environment or ambient tools. The runner passes every path a check needs explicitly. Any choice between a preferred tool and a fallback is recorded in the check's output, and a silent fallback counts as a defect. The reader applies this default when a request changes how checks run, so it need not ask.
proposed_request: Make Athena's test checks run with nextest reliably. Pass the directory holding the pinned tools to every check explicitly, by adding ATHENA_HOME or the resolved tools path to the environment a check receives. Each test check must record and print which runner it used (nextest or cargo test), so a fallback to cargo test is never silent. Keep nextest as the chosen runner and keep the measured timing numbers from the earlier correction. Doctests still run with cargo test --doc. Acceptance: a check run in the cleared sandbox environment uses nextest and prints that it did; with the tools path removed, the check prints that it used cargo test; the existing tests still pass.
